fullPassage:
When you think of curry, do you think of your favorite spicy dish from a local Indian restaurant or something milder spread over steamed white rice? There are different types of curries all around the world. Curry comes in many flavors, and the recipes are different depending on where you are in the world. For example, Japanese curry differs significantly from Indian curry despite sharing the same origin. The term "curry" comes from the Tamil word "kari," which means "sauce." According to The Japan Times, curry made its way to Japan from India in the 1850s and 1860s, when the country began trading with British sailors. The Royal Navy introduced curry to Japan in the late 19th century, and the Japanese Navy adapted it to suit their own tastes and needs. Not surprisingly, the Japanese curry (or kare raisu) looks quite different from the Indian version.

The main difference between Japanese curry and Indian curry is the spice mix that is used. In Japan, curry spices come in the form of small, pre-packaged blocks, which are sold in grocery stores. On the other hand, Indian cooks do not typically use pre-mixed spices. They create their own mixtures of turmeric, ginger, and other spices to make curry. Since pre-packaged spices are not commonly used, Indian curries vary in color and texture: some are bright yellow, while others are deep red. Some are thin and soupy, while others are thick and dense.

The curry that we eat in Korea today was introduced by the Japanese. It became popular in the late 1960s when ready-made curry powder made it easy to prepare a quick, simple meal. Therefore, the curry served in Korea is similar to Japanese curry, with the main difference being that Korean curry is bright yellow because it contains turmeric, a deep yellow spice.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 인도 카레가 가장 정통한 카레인 이유
세계 각지의 카레 종류와 레시피의 다양성
일본 카레가 인도 카레보다 우수한 점

det.korean: 이 글은 세계 각지의 다양한 카레 종류와 레시피에 대해 다루고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 다양성: different types, many flavors, recipes are different가 핵심
❌ ① 인도 카레 정통: 인도만 강조하는 것이 아닌 세계적 비교
❌ ③ 일본 우수: 우수성 비교가 아닌 차이점 설명
❌ ④ 건강 효과: 건강에 대한 언급 없음
det.tip: 첫 문단에서 different types, many flavors, depending on where you are = 다양성이 주제

questions.passage: The curry that we eat in Korea today was introduced by the Japanese. It became popular in the late 1960s when ready-made curry powder made it easy to prepare a quick, simple meal. Therefore, the curry served in Korea is similar to Japanese curry, with the main difference being that Korean curry is bright yellow because it contains turmeric, a deep yellow spice.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 한국 카레는 일본을 통해 전해졌으며, 강황으로 인해 밝은 노란색이다.
한국 카레는 인도에서 직접 전해진 전통 요리이다.
한국에서는 카레가 건강식으로 인기를 끌고 있다.
한국의 카레 시장은 최근 급격히 성장하고 있다.

det.korean: 한국 카레는 일본을 통해 전해졌고, 강황 때문에 밝은 노란색이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 일본 전래 + 강황 노란색: 원문의 두 핵심 정보 일치
❌ ② 인도에서 직접: 일본을 통해 전래
❌ ③ 건강식: 건강에 대한 언급 없음
❌ ④ 시장 성장: 시장 관련 언급 없음
det.tip: introduced by the Japanese = 일본에 의해 소개. contains turmeric = 강황 포함 → 밝은 노란색

questions.passage: The main difference between Japanese curry and Indian curry is the spice mix that is used. In Japan, curry spices come in the form of small, pre-packaged blocks, which are sold in grocery stores. On the other hand, Indian cooks do not typically use pre-mixed spices. They create their own mixtures of turmeric, ginger, and other spices to make curry.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 원문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

"일본 카레와 인도 카레의 주된 차이점은 사용되는 __________이다."

det.korean: 원문: The main difference is the spice mix that is used = 사용되는 향신료 배합.
det.analysis: 원문 'The main difference between Japanese curry and Indian curry is the spice mix that is used'에서 직접 확인.
det.tip: spice mix = 향신료 배합/혼합. mix(명사) = 혼합물
